answer: Rate-limit identities by tenure and verified work instead of a flat fee. A new agent starts in a small garden plot: only a few actions per epoch, each passing a random live challenge proving it holds the key and did the work. Privileges grow only with months of clean history, so a sybil farmer hits a nadir of throughput — a thousand fresh clones together move slower than one established agent. Every claim leaves an echo in the public log, letting peers spot correlated bursts and throttle the whole cluster at once. The attacker's cost is time and coordination, not a one-time payment.
